policy: Endpoint reconciliation manifest v3. The route list contains application entry points only; shared config/helper files are excluded. Candidate methods are reconciled against source-level guards where present, but no route is runtime-verified by this manifest. Each route still requires authenticated staging tests for anonymous access, wrong methods, CSRF, capabilities, workspace/record scope, workflow state, idempotency, transaction effects, and audit outcomes. A source marker is evidence for review, not proof of enforcement. This manifest is not runtime authorization enforcement and does not constitute a production-readiness certification.

routes.capability_description: ticket ownership and destination office authority
routes.enforcement_notes: AICS office-reassignment ticket creation rechecks requester scope, current office, destination validity, and captured record version under row lock.
POST capability is rechecked; edit scope and workflow state are revalidated under SELECT FOR UPDATE before updating.

AICS direct deletion is POST+CSRF, requires edit_records, locks the record, rechecks office scope and LPGMA WAITING/admin policy, writes the complete payload to shared trash, deletes and audits in one transaction. Legacy restore action is rejected; restore is only through administrator trash workflow.
AICS revision-ticket creation rechecks office scope and captured record version under row lock; proposals remain pending until administrator decision.

AICS approved delete tickets lock the pending ticket and linked record, require matching base record version, archive the complete payload, then delete within the same transaction; ticket decision and audit remain linked.

AICS restoration is admin+edit_records only, POST+CSRF, uses a named sequence lock and transaction, locks the archive row, assigns a new control number/date/status, atomically marks restored and audits. Runtime database tests remain pending.
